text:
Sam Bennett has two Stanley Cups and a Conn Smythe, and this season he has five goals in 18 games. The shape of it is the worry: three of his five goals came in one night against Seattle in October, and his ice time is down almost three minutes over the last ten games.

Some of the quiet is bad luck. Florida has scored 5.9 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, which has cost him assists (he has three). The Panthers hold 55% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) when he's out there. That's a good player having a frustrating month.

He's still the guy who draws the other team's best, per Evolving-Hockey, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting 2.2 shots per 60 off passes across the slot or from behind the net, the best kind. The flip side: he takes more penalties than he draws. Our projection sees about 25 goals, and we'd watch his minutes before his points.
